key_points: CUCM is the call-control server; phones and gateways register with it and it sets up calls.
The Publisher holds the read/write configuration database, and Subscribers hold read-only copies for redundancy and call processing.
Phones obtain their IP address from DHCP and their configuration file from a TFTP server, commonly through DHCP option 150.
A directory number (DN) is placed in a partition, and a calling search space (CSS) is an ordered list of partitions a device may search.
Dial-plan patterns use wildcards such as X (one digit 0-9) and ! (one or more digits) to match dialed numbers.
A caller can reach a DN only when the caller's CSS includes the partition that contains that DN.
guide.explanation: Cisco Unified Communications Manager (CUCM) provides call control for IP phones and gateways, and it uses a Publisher for configuration and Subscribers for redundancy and call processing. Endpoints such as IP phones get their address from DHCP, their settings from TFTP, and then register with CUCM before they can place calls. Dial plans are built from directory numbers grouped into partitions, and calling search spaces decide which partitions each device can reach. Source: Network Applications I course outline, Outline week 14: Cisco Unified Communications Manager (CUCM), architecture, endpoints, dial plans, partitions, and calling search spaces.
guide.example: Suppose a route pattern is $2XXX$, where each X matches one digit 0-9. The number $2475$ matches because it has four digits and starts with 2. The number $3475$ does not match because it starts with 3, and $24759$ does not match because it has five digits.

questions.question: Which CUCM server holds the read/write master copy of the configuration database?
options: Subscriber
Publisher
TFTP server
Media resource
questions.explanation: The Publisher holds the read/write master database, and Subscribers keep read-only copies. Source: Network Applications I course outline, Outline week 14: Cisco Unified Communications Manager (CUCM), architecture.

questions.question: Which DHCP option is commonly used to tell an IP phone the address of its TFTP server?
options: Option 3
Option 6
Option 51
Option 150
questions.explanation: DHCP option 150 provides the TFTP server address that a phone uses to download its configuration file. Source: Network Applications I course outline, Outline week 14: Cisco Unified Communications Manager (CUCM), endpoints.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a partition in a CUCM dial plan?
options: To group directory numbers that share the same reachability
To set the codec used on a physical switch port
To store the ring tone file for a phone
To define the voicemail PIN for each user
questions.answer: To group directory numbers that share the same reachability
questions.explanation: Partitions group directory numbers and route patterns with the same reachability, and calling search spaces then select which partitions a device may search. Source: Network Applications I course outline, Outline week 14: Cisco Unified Communications Manager (CUCM), dial plans and partitions.

questions.question: Which definition best describes a calling search space (CSS)?
options: An ordered list of partitions that a device searches when it places a call
A single directory number assigned to one phone
A list of codecs allowed between two sites
A DHCP scope that assigns addresses to phones
questions.answer: An ordered list of partitions that a device searches when it places a call
questions.explanation: A calling search space is an ordered list of partitions, and the device searches those partitions in order to find a match for the dialed number. Source: Network Applications I course outline, Outline week 14: Cisco Unified Communications Manager (CUCM), calling search spaces.

questions.question: Phone A has a CSS that contains only partition Internal. Directory number 2001 is in partition Lobby. Can Phone A call 2001?
options: Yes, because all directory numbers are reachable by default
Yes, because partitions are ignored for internal calls
No, because partition Lobby is not in Phone A's CSS
No, because the call would need a DHCP option 150 entry
questions.answer: No, because partition Lobby is not in Phone A's CSS
questions.explanation: A device can reach a directory number only if the partition containing that number is in the device's calling search space. Since Lobby is missing, the call fails. Source: Network Applications I course outline, Outline week 14: Cisco Unified Communications Manager (CUCM), partitions and calling search spaces.

questions.question: In a dial-plan pattern, what does the wildcard X match?
options: Any single digit from 0 to 9
One or more digits of any length
Any single digit from 1 to 9 only
Only the letter X in the dialed string
questions.explanation: In CUCM patterns, X matches any single digit from 0 to 9, so the pattern 2XXX matches four-digit numbers that start with 2. Source: Network Applications I course outline, Outline week 14: Cisco Unified Communications Manager (CUCM), dial plans.

questions.question: Which SIP message does an IP phone send to CUCM to register itself?
options: INVITE
REGISTER
OPTIONS
BYE
questions.explanation: A SIP phone sends a REGISTER message to CUCM to register its contact and identity. INVITE starts a call, OPTIONS queries capabilities, and BYE ends a call. Source: Network Applications I course outline, Outline week 14: Cisco Unified Communications Manager (CUCM), endpoints.

questions.question: Which settings are grouped together in a CUCM device pool?
options: Date/time group and region
Voicemail PIN and user password
Ring tone file and wallpaper image
Partition name and route pattern
questions.explanation: A device pool groups shared settings such as the date/time group and region for a set of endpoints. Partitions and route patterns are dial-plan objects, not device pool settings. Source: Network Applications I course outline, Outline week 14: Cisco Unified Communications Manager (CUCM), endpoints.
